jobs.location: Victorville, California, United States; Hesperia, California, United States; Apple Valley, California, United States
jobs.description:
Job Overview:
*Relocation Assistance Eligible*

The Aseptic Whole Line Performance Leader is accountable for the safe, reliable, and efficient performance of the complete Sidel and Krones aseptic production line—from blow molding through filling, capping, conveying, labeling, packaging, and palletizing. This role owns execution and results across the line, including safety, quality, customer fill rate, case attainment, OEE2, unplanned and planned downtime, waste, and cost per case.

The Aseptic Whole Line Performance Leader will establish and execute the operating strategy for the Sidel and Krones aseptic line, aligning Operations, Maintenance, Quality, Engineering, Planning, and OEM support to deliver sustained top-quartile whole-line performance.

The role leads daily line execution, loss elimination, reliability improvement, operating discipline, and capability development across the entire aseptic process. Responsibilities include setting performance priorities, coordinating shift and functional resources, leading tiered performance reviews, removing systemic constraints, ensuring operational readiness for product, package, and equipment changes, and sustaining improvements through standard work, preventive maintenance, centerlining, root cause problem solving, and operator and technician skill development.

The Aseptic Whole Line Performance Leader is a key member of the Plant Leadership Team and serves as the single point of accountability for Sidel and Krones aseptic line performance. The role connects Operations, Maintenance, Quality, Engineering, Planning, and OEM partners; establishes clear priorities and owners; escalates barriers; and ensures corrective actions are completed and sustained. This position reports to the Plant Manager.

Location: Victorville, CA

What you will do:
- Own Whole-Line Performance for the Sidel and Krones Aseptic Line
- Develop and lead a cross-functional rapid response team capable of diagnosing, containing, and permanently eliminating losses across the complete aseptic line.
- Serve as the line owner between CAPEX teams, OEMs, and the plant for new installations, ensuring design integration, operational readiness, vertical ramp-up, and sustained performance across the connected line.

- Lead capital projects, executing with excellence and vertical ramp ups.

- Collaborate with site leadership to ensure Operations Model labor standards are being met for maintenance teams.
- Lead and deliver maintenance and reliability related productivity projects.
- Responsible for functional area network dashboards, and corrective actions to drive KPI improvement. Drives sustainable improvements to positively impact the achievement of Key Performance Indicators (KPI’s), Manage SRM Dashboards, and Scorecards relative to cost, productivity and on-time delivery by optimizing labor and production capabilities.

- Annual bonus based on performance and eligibility

- Experience with aseptic filling is required
- Bachelor's degree in a Science, Technical/Engineering preferred. Master’s degree in business or engineering management a plus
- Project management certification a plus
- Minimum of 10 years of experience in a combination of manufacturing and engineering

jobs.description:
Job Overview:
Director of Sales Operations - Los Angeles, CA

The Director of Sales Operations drives strategic analysis, execution, and organizational development to achieve financial and non-financial goals in addition to creating a lean mindset throughout the assigned DSD facility to improve safety, productivity and performance through standardization and process discipline.
This role is accountable for the development of field personnel and achieving performance objectives in Safety, Quality, Delivery, Productivity, and Growth.

Through active leadership the Director of Sales Operations will:
- Drive accident and injury reduction and vehicle accident reduction targets in assigned facility.
- Provide case management and follow up on all SAFE system cases and ensure that proper accident investigations, classifications, follow-ups and Root Cause Counter Measures are determined.
- Drive Safety First culture by ensuring monthly Regulatory and Safety in Motion training is completed by all employees and Safety Playbooks are implemented with 100% compliance.
- Ensure regulatory compliance by conducting OSHA style audits and ensuring closure of any regulatory gaps to achieve 100% regulatory compliance.
- Drive increase in On Time and Accurate (OTA) score by addressing routing and delivery issues as well as ensuring pick accuracy exceeds 99.8% through full execution of Voice Pick standards and compliance to daily checklist and reduction of haulbacks.
- Drive reduction in waste by ensuring assigned facility meets or exceeds break/shrink/obsolescence goals on a cost per case basis.
- Ensure labor costs in the warehouse and delivery operations of assigned facility meet or beat plan on a cost per case basis by driving home Warehouse University principles, including the deployment of the Warehouse Self Assessment tool.
- Communicate regularly with internal and external partners and customers through weekly operations calls and as needed meetings to ensure high level of customer service is maintained.
- Drive facility-level engagement plans and ensure employee engagement in large teams and/or across many sites.
- P&L Responsibility: Responsible for the management of the facility
- Ensure high performance results of your team:
- Foster a culture of trust and wellbeing that prioritizes the team and values employee contributions.
- Drive a shared vision with clear goals and accountability, supported by regular conversations to maximize talent.
- Embrace diverse perspectives to foster innovation, learning from both successes and failures.
- Establish a safe environment where team members are motivated, heard, and aligned with clear expectations.

- Travel required as needed

The ideal candidate will possess:
- A proven track record of improving safety results, successful continuous improvement initiatives and superior cost and management results.
- Strong leadership and communication skills; excellent verbal and written skills along with experience presenting to regional leadership teams, local leadership teams, and frontline employees.
- A background in the management of Warehouse, Inventory and Delivery.
- Knowledge of Department of Transportation (DOT), Federal, State and Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) compliance.
- Experience working with MHE, (material handling equipment) understand warehouse capacity requirements, building, loading, and delivery principals, FIFO and logistics principals.

Total Rewards:
- $160,000 - $180,000 / year
- Actual placement within the compensation range may vary depending on experience, skills, and other factors

- Annual bonus based on performance and eligibility

Requirements:

- Strong understanding of Department of Transportation (DOT), Federal, State and Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) compliance
- Experience presenting to executive leadership teams, local leadership teams, and front line employees

jobs.description:
Job Overview:
Summer 2027 Intern – Continuous Improvement

As a 2027 Summer Intern at Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP), you will have the opportunity to work in a challenging, highly technical and dynamic Manufacturing and warehouse environment that produces some of KDP’s most recognized beverages. In this role you will have the opportunity to help provide insight on the future of how we move finished goods within our local footprint, ultimately improving our time to market.

This role is aligned to the Beverage Operating Unit.

Shift/Schedule:
- The KDP 2027 Summer Internship Program will run from June 7 – August 13, 2027
- Full-time; 40 hours per week
- Monday-Friday
- 8:00am until 5:00pm
- In-person in the Aspers, PA facility

As a Continuous Improvement intern you will:
- Analyze the current flow of materials and products across a multi-building distribution and warehouse network to identify inefficiencies and improvement opportunities.
- Gain exposure to project management activities, including project planning, vendor coordination, sourcing initiatives, and oversight of operational improvement projects.
- Leverage data analytics to evaluate inventory placement and develop strategic recommendations for optimizing product storage within the existing facility footprint.
- Partner with operations teams to understand daily workflows, identify process bottlenecks, and recommend solutions that improve efficiency, productivity, and overall operational flow.
- Participate in continuous improvement initiatives by collecting and analyzing operational data to support informed decision-making and process optimization efforts.
- Collaborate cross-functionally with supply chain, warehouse, and logistics teams to enhance material movement, storage utilization, and operational effectiveness.

Elements of the KDP 2027 Internship Program include:
- Engaging and partnering on innovative projects to gain experience in a fast paced, cross functional team environment
- Receive mentor support for your professional development
- Participate in meet & greets and lunch & learns with KDP executives and other organization leaders
- Receive professional development training such as networking, professional skills development and presenting
- Complete a project from start to finish and present it and your takeaways to your team, department, and senior leaders to highlight your project work and impact on the business

- $31.00/ hour
- Paid bi-weekly
- $2,500 Sign-on Bonus, paid within first 30 days of employment

Stagiaire LEAP hiver 2027 – Excellence opérationnelle VHCS

Aperçu
Nous sommes à la recherche d’un ou d’une stagiaire en processus d’audit d’inventaire, rigoureux·euse et analytique, pour soutenir le développement et la mise en œuvre d’un programme formel d’audit d’inventaire au sein de l’équipe Excellence opérationnelle. Ce stage visera à renforcer les contrôles d’inventaire, améliorer l’exactitude des stocks, identifier les écarts de processus et créer des outils et de la documentation reproductibles afin de soutenir l’efficacité opérationnelle à long terme.
La personne sélectionnée contribuera à définir les procédures d’audit, à soutenir les audits pilotes, à analyser les écarts, à documenter les constats et à proposer des améliorations de processus visant à réduire les risques opérationnels et financiers.

Quart de travail / Horaire
- Dates du programme : 4 janvier au 30 avril 2027
- Lieu : Montréal, QC
- Mode hybride; 3 jours au bureau
- Du lundi au vendredi

Les éléments du programme de stage LEAP comprennent :
- Participer à des projets novateurs et collaborer avec différentes équipes afin d’acquérir de l’expérience dans un environnement dynamique et interfonctionnel.
- Bénéficier du soutien d’un mentor pour favoriser votre développement professionnel.
- Participer à des rencontres informelles et à des dîners-conférences avec des membres de la direction de KDP et d’autres leaders de l’organisation.
- Recevoir de la formation en développement professionnel, notamment sur le réseautage, les compétences professionnelles et les présentations.
- Réaliser un projet du début à la fin, puis le présenter, ainsi que vos apprentissages, à votre équipe, à votre service et à des leaders seniors afin de mettre en valeur votre travail et son impact sur l’entreprise.

Principales responsabilités
- Concevoir et soutenir un processus d’audit d’inventaire reproductible, incluant la méthodologie de comptage cyclique, les processus de rapprochement, les seuils et les normes de production de rapports.
- Définir les objectifs, la portée, la fréquence, les emplacements ainsi que les UGS ou familles de produits ciblées par les audits.
- Développer des outils pratiques, modèles, listes de vérification et documents de suivi pour soutenir l’exécution et la documentation des audits.
- Planifier et exécuter des audits pilotes dans certaines zones d’entrepôt ou catégories d’inventaire afin de valider le processus proposé.
- Rapprocher les décomptes physiques avec les données des systèmes et identifier les écarts liés aux erreurs de comptage, aux articles mal placés, aux erreurs de saisie, aux dommages ou aux lacunes de processus.
- Analyser les résultats d’audit afin de cerner les tendances, les causes fondamentales et les occasions d’amélioration.
- Créer une documentation claire sur les processus, des procédures opérationnelles normalisées, des guides de démarrage rapide et du matériel de formation.
- Soutenir les séances de formation pratique avec les équipes d’entrepôt et des opérations, et recueillir leurs commentaires afin de peaufiner le processus.
- Définir des indicateurs clés de performance pour suivre l’exactitude de l’inventaire, les taux d’écart, les délais de rapprochement et l’efficacité globale des audits.
- Recommander des fréquences de production de rapports, des formats de tableaux de bord et des initiatives d’amélioration continue afin de soutenir le contrôle de l’inventaire à long terme.

Exigences
- Être actuellement aux études dans un programme de baccalauréat en gestion de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, gestion des opérations, génie industriel, administration des affaires, logistique, systèmes d’information, analytique de données ou dans un domaine connexe.
- Excellente maîtrise d’Excel ou de Google Sheets, incluant les formules, les tableaux croisés dynamiques, RECHERCHEV/RECHERCHEX et la mise en forme conditionnelle.
- Compétences de base en analyse de données requises; la connaissance de SQL, Python, des systèmes ERP/WMS, de Power BI, Tableau ou Looker est considérée comme un atout.
- Grand souci du détail et engagement envers l’exactitude.
- Solides compétences en résolution de problèmes analytiques et capacité à investiguer les causes fondamentales.
- Excellentes compétences en communication écrite et verbale.
- Aisance à travailler dans des environnements opérationnels ou d’entrepôt.
- Bonne gestion du temps et capacité à respecter les échéanciers liés aux projets ou aux audits pilotes.
- Esprit de collaboration et ouverture à recevoir de la rétroaction afin d’améliorer les processus.
- Fiabilité, ponctualité et capacité à respecter les procédures de santé et sécurité en entrepôt.
- Expérience avec les décomptes physiques, les audits, les procédures opérationnelles normalisées, les listes de vérification ou la documentation de processus, un atout important.
- Capacité à être sur place pour les décomptes d’inventaire, les séances de formation et certaines activités physiques occasionnelles, comme marcher, rester debout ou soulever de petites boîtes.

Exigences linguistiques
La maîtrise du français et de l’anglais, à l’oral et à l’écrit, est requise. Toute autre compétence linguistique pertinente aux environnements d’entrepôt, d’opérations ou de fournisseurs est considérée comme un atout.

Overview:
We are seeking a detail-oriented and analytical Inventory Audit Process Intern to support the development and implementation of a formal inventory audit program within the Operational Excellence team. This internship will focus on strengthening inventory controls, improving stock accuracy, identifying process gaps, and creating repeatable tools and documentation that support long-term operational efficiency.
The selected intern will help define audit procedures, support pilot audits, analyze discrepancies, document findings, and contribute to process improvements that reduce operational and financial risk.

Shift / Schedule
- Program Dates: January 4 – April 30, 2027
- Location: Montréal, QC
- Hybrid; 3 days in office
- Monday–Friday

Elements of the LEAP Internship Program include:
- Engaging and partnering on innovative projects to gain experience in a fast paced, cross functional team environment
- Receive mentor support for your professional development
- Participate in meet & greets and lunch & learns with KDP executives and other organization leaders
- Receive professional development training such as networking, professional skills development and presenting
- Complete a project from start to finish and present it and your takeaways to your team, department, and senior leaders to highlight your project work and impact on the business

Key Responsibilities
- Design and support a repeatable inventory audit process, including cycle count methodology, reconciliation workflows, thresholds, and reporting standards.
- Define audit objectives, scope, frequency, locations, and targeted SKUs or product families.
- Develop practical tools, templates, checklists, and tracking documents to support audit execution and documentation.
- Plan and execute pilot audits in selected warehouse zones or inventory categories to validate the proposed process.
- Reconcile physical counts against system records and identify discrepancies related to miscounts, misplacements, entry errors, damage, or process gaps.
- Analyze audit results to identify patterns, root causes, and opportunities for improvement.
- Create clear process documentation, standard operating procedures, quick-start guides, and training materials.
- Support hands-on training sessions with warehouse and operations teams and gather feedback to refine the process.
- Define key performance indicators to monitor inventory accuracy, discrepancy rates, reconciliation timing, and overall audit effectiveness.
- Recommend reporting cadences, dashboard layouts, and continuous improvement initiatives to support long-term inventory control.

Requirements
- Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations Management, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, Logistics, Information Systems, Data Analytics, or related fields.
- Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills, including formulas, pivot tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, and conditional formatting.
- Basic data analysis skills are required; familiarity with SQL, Python, ERP/WMS systems, Power BI, Tableau, or Looker is considered an asset.
- Strong attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.
- Analytical problem-solving skills and ability to investigate root causes.
- Clear written and verbal communication skills.
- Comfort working in operational or warehouse environments.
- Strong time management skills and ability to meet pilot or project deadlines.
- Collaborative mindset with a willingness to receive feedback and iterate on processes.
- Reliable, punctual, and able to follow warehouse safety procedures.
- Experience with physical counts, audits, SOPs, checklists, or process documentation is a strong plus.
- Ability to be on-site for inventory counts, training sessions, and occasional physical activity such as walking, standing, or lifting small boxes.

Language Requirements:
Proficiency in English and French, both written and verbal, is required. Additional language skills relevant to warehouse, operations, or supplier environments are considered an asset.
